    - ASK 587, A JUDGE IS NOT SENT BACK, COUNTED OR REMOVED FOR A DEFECT OF THE ENGINE'S OWN MAKING (one write, engine and child; Shared Library, both copies; Reread Record, Alt Reread Record and R2 Alt Reread Record). Why: in run 42071 seats were removed on defects of the engine's own form. Judge lines of 1,685 and 1,721 characters were stored and checked as 1,500-character copies, so their DECIDES to WHY IT FAILS tail was not read, and a cure was spliced into the cut copy; a KEEP that quoted the answering side's own sentence was refused because the other side had quoted that sentence; a KEYSTONE was asked to name a collision line the judge had not written; a second reading reversed the grade the first reading had asked for; and a RESULT was written CHALLENGER WINS beside a counted challenger break.
      1. A, the whole line: no stored flagged_line is cut (20 library lines, 5 MAP strings and the three Reread Record nodes). The five prompt builders that showed a line cut to 1,500 or 1,600 characters with " [...]" show it whole. A line that reaches the E-COL layer check ending " [...]" makes no item: it is NOT READ, never UNCURED.
      2. B, own words: in the E-COL KEEP reading, a 6-word run is passed over as quoted only when it stands inside quotation marks in a round and the answering side did not also write it outside its own quotation marks. Still passed over: a run the answering side wrote only inside its own quotation marks.
      3. C1, the keystone label: when the judge's text has no line "D<k> vs C<m>" for the keystone link, the pkgLAY KEYSTONE item demands no collision label, in the scan and in the cure. Its [L1] check is unchanged.
      4. C2, the second reading: an E-REREAD DISAGREE on a changed KEYSTONE (E-KEY) or RESULT (E-RES) word that equals the first reading's "(right: X)" is labelled RECORD-ONLY and adds nothing to drv_uncured.
      5. D, the RESULT: a counted closing-contradiction break of the CHALLENGER that no collision line names enters every RESULT path as one collision graded CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN: the AUDIT v25 recompute, the AUDIT v61 ENGINE RESULT tag (listed in its INPUTS as "C<k> (CLOSE-CONTRADICTION, no collision line names it) CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN") and the gate recompute. The AUDIT v25 line prints "STANDING INPUTS: DEFENDER conceded <c>, CHALLENGER conceded <c>; RESULT INPUTS: counted breaks no collision line names: DEFENDER <n>, CHALLENGER <n>". The standing is unchanged: it reads the conceded count only. The defender side is not added.
      6. E, the removal reason: UNREAD COUNTED LINE is tallied only from a line that opens with an audit mark ("[AUDIT v<n>:"), so a send-back item line that holds the words "counted in drv_uncured" is not tallied. This changes the removal-reason text only, not a removal.
      7. Limits: a false closing-contradiction flag against the challenger now also keeps CHALLENGER WINS from a BROKEN verdict, and gives DEFENDER WINS on HELD by the same clause of section 8. Not shown by a run: each item waits for a run that holds its case. Shown offline on stored judgments 1272, 1273 and 1274 of run 42071.
      8. Marks for the next run: a flagged_line over 1,500 characters is stored whole; no E-COL send-back reads "no deciding step" on a line that carries "-- WHY IT FAILS:"; no pkgLAY KEYSTONE item reads "names no collision line of D<k>" when the judge wrote no "D<k> vs C" line; an E-REREAD row whose changed line carries the first reading's grade reads RECORD-ONLY; an AUDIT v25 line with "counted as one CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN" has a RECOMPUTED RESULT that is not CHALLENGER WINS, and the same seat's last AUDIT v61 WORD is not CHALLENGER WINS; removed_rules carries no UNREAD COUNTED LINE from a SEND-BACK ITEM line.

14.0.old:
- THE QUESTION ROUND (QR Ask Build, QR Check, QR Final, QR Merge): runs only in a dry regrade (question_trial true, dry true); running it in a live debate needs the operator's approval.
    - The ask carries the watch-and-question paragraph; the JSON form takes optional earlier_round and earlier_quote. qrCheck keeps ruling 415's checks and, only when an earlier field holds text, checks that the round is that debater's closing round (CR4 or DR4), earlier_round is one of its earlier rounds, the earlier quote is word for word in that round, and the new-verse check reads the earlier quote too. The debater sees both quotes. The judges' text labels a CONTRADICTION QUESTION with both quotes.
14.0.new:
- THE QUESTION ROUND (ASK 588; Init Seats, QR Ask Build, QR Check, QR Final, the answer nodes QR Answer and QR Answer D and C, QR Merge): runs on every fresh run unless the run body sends question_trial:false; in a regrade it runs only when question_trial:true is sent.
    - Order: after Panel Build and before the judges judge, each of the three panel judges puts one question to each debater (six questions); each debater answers; every judge then reads all six questions and answers.
    - The question: the ask gives the fixed forms MEANING, FIT and AGREE, and keeps the watch-for-contradictions paragraph, which steers the judge to AGREE. The judge gives the round, the quotation and the form; with MEANING a term, with FIT a verse; only an AGREE question takes earlier_round and earlier_quote, and its quotation is from the closing round. The program writes the question. MEANING: `What does "<term>" in this passage mean?` FIT: `How does this passage fit <verse>?` AGREE, where a debater's closing round contradicts its own earlier round: `How do these two passages agree?`
    - Checks before a question is sent (qrCheck in QR Check): the round is that debater's; the form is one of the three; the quotation stands word for word in that round (8 characters or more); the term stands in the quotation; the verse is named in the quotation; the closing and earlier quotations of an AGREE question stand in their rounds; no verse is one the debater has not cited. A failed question is returned to its judge once.
    - The answer: from the debater's own seat model by its own route (the direct Anthropic route or OpenRouter), the defender first, then the challenger; at most 250 words.
    - The block: QR Merge writes one block, "=== QUESTION ROUND === ... === END QUESTION ROUND ===", before "DEBATE TRANSCRIPT" in each judge body. Its rule reads: "Each answer explains only the passage it quotes and is read with the round it came from, as an explanation of that passage. Every quotation you write in your lines, and every concession you count, comes from the eight rounds of the transcript ([CR1] to [DR4]): an answer is never quoted as a round, and a concession is counted only where a round makes it." Every later turn of a judge reads the bodies that carry the block: the send-back, the gate, the late gate, cures 1 to 3, the reserve, the alternates in the engine and in the child, and the panel check.
    - A fault: any fault in the round skips the round and never stops the run. The round is also skipped when a panel judge seat is not an OpenRouter seat, or when a debater's family is neither Anthropic nor OpenRouter.
    - Record: none is stored. Build Save Body holds a line "[QUESTION ROUND v1: ...]" for review_notes, but on a live run Build Save Body runs before the round, so the line never writes. The judges receive the questions and answers; the run row does not hold them.
    - An AGREE question is a contradiction candidate for Judge Contradiction Build.
    - Limits: the enforcer turn (Judge Enforcer Build) does not see the block; the single judge does not get it; an answer is never counted as a round. Not shown by a run.
    - Cost (estimate): about 0.35 to 0.6 million added input tokens per run, and several minutes.
    - ONE CONTINUATION PASS (switch qr_follow, on whenever the round runs unless qr_follow:false is sent; QR Follow Build, QR Follow Ask, QR Follow Final and the QR Follow D and C answer nodes): after the six answers each judge reads them all and may put at most one continuation to each debater, only on a question ANOTHER judge put to that debater. The judge keeps its own question: Q1 to Q6 stay, and continuations are numbered Q7 and after. The judge gives Q<n> and copies the words of that question, or of the passage it quotes, that the answer left open (8 characters or more, word for word); the program writes `Your answer to Q<n> did not answer: "<the words>". Please explain that part.` NONE asks nothing. Dropped and recorded, with no return: a continuation of the judge's own question; of a question not put to that debater; of a question with no answer; of a continuation; a second one to the same debater; one whose words are not found. The debater answers by its own route. The continuations stand in the same block, each marked "FOLLOW-UP to Q<n>". A continuation is not a contradiction candidate. A fault in the pass keeps the first pass as it is and records the skip. With the switch off, the judges receive the block without continuations. Cost: up to 3 more judge calls and 6 more answers. Not shown by a run.
